question: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announced its monetary policy on 9th October 2024, maintaining the repo rate at ____________.
solution:
The correct answer is__** 6.5%.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announced its monetary policy on 9th October 2024.
 
• The RBI decided to maintain the repo rate at 6.5% (0.065) during this announcement.
 
• The decision to hold the repo rate steady is often influenced by the need to control inflation while supporting economic growth.
 
• The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends money to commercial banks, impacting the overall interest rates in the economy.
 
• This policy decision is part of the RBI's broader strategy to manage the economy's liquidity and monetary conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Repo Rate**

 
 
• The repo rate is the rate at which the central bank of a country (RBI in India) lends money to commercial banks in the event of any shortfall of funds.
 
• It is used by monetary authorities to control inflation.
 
• A higher repo rate can help to curb inflation, while a lower rate can help to stimulate economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Reverse Repo Rate**
 
 
• It is the rate at which the central bank borrows money from commercial banks.
 
• It is used to control the money supply in the economy.
 
• Currently, it stands lower than the repo rate to ensure liquidity remains in the system.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**
 
 
• The MPC is responsible for fixing the benchmark interest rate in India.
 
• It consists of six members, including three officials from the RBI and three external members nominated by the government.
 
• Decisions are made based on a majority vote with the RBI Governor having a casting vote in case of a tie.
 
 
 
• **Inflation Targeting**
 
 
• Inflation targeting refers to the monetary policy strategy used by the RBI to keep inflation within a specified range.
 
• The current inflation target set by the government is 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2%.
 
• This strategy aims to provide a stable economic environment conducive to sustained growth.
